name: Disformal-Displaced Bimetric MOND (DDBM)
claimed_mechanism: The theory employs Hassan-Rosen ghost-free bigravity to supply a second dynamical metric that evades the single-metric slip-lock theorem (DC-013). While the massive graviton provides the necessary off-ray lensing correction to achieve the MOND ratio, the MOND acceleration dependence is injected via a non-linear helicity-0 potential. This architecture explicitly exits the local single-metric dead classes and bypasses the P7 strong-coupling wall by relying on a bimetric kinetic normalization.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the bimetric sector generates an f(R)-like slip ratio that is structurally forced to eta=1 by the specific massless limit of the HR potential. The MOND force law emerges from the non-linear coupling of the chi scalar to the curvature, reproducing mu=1-e^-y while the massive graviton ensures the correct MOND lensing ratio without a preferred frame.
inequivalence_argument: This is structurally distinct from DC-001 (which is limited to single-metric theories) and DC-013 (which is a no-go for frame-free single-metric slip). It avoids DC-002 (no 6-DOF aether) and DC-014 (no stiff vector). It addresses the P7 collision by using a bimetric kinetic structure where the lensing carrier (h metric) and the MOND strength (chi potential) are decoupled from the screened preferred-frame response.
